%% --- Detection AUROC per model (grouped bar): LPP vs semantic entropy -------
\begin{figure}[t]
  \centering
  \includegraphics[width=0.95\linewidth]{fig_auroc_v2.pdf}
  \caption{Detection AUROC against executable gold-ambiguity, per model and pooled.
  The latent-premise-pinning detector ($H_{\mathrm{ctx}}$, LPP) separates ambiguous from
  unambiguous prompts (pooled $0.895$), while same-prompt semantic entropy
  ($H_{\mathrm{seed}}$) sits near chance (pooled $0.581$). The requirements-probing
  baseline is also strong (pooled $0.810$, dashed). The pattern is consistent across all
  six models (three families, two tiers).}
  \label{fig:auroc-comparison-v2}
\end{figure}

%% --- Danger quadrant (real per-item data) -----------------------------------
\begin{figure}[t]
  \centering
  \includegraphics[width=0.72\linewidth]{fig_danger_quadrant_v2.pdf}
  \caption{The danger quadrant, on confirmatory benchmark data. Each point is one of the
  54 pre-registered items at its pooled per-item mean of $H_{\mathrm{seed}}$ (semantic
  entropy) and $H_{\mathrm{ctx}}$ (latent-premise pinning), coloured by executable
  gold-ambiguity. \textbf{25 of 33 ($0.758$) AMB$+$ items} fall in the low-$H_{\mathrm{seed}}$
  ($\le\!\tau_s{=}0.5$) $\wedge$ high-$H_{\mathrm{ctx}}$ danger region, where semantic
  entropy is blind; AMB$-$ controls stay near the origin. Points coinciding at identical
  discrete values are jittered slightly for visibility; no point's underlying value is
  altered.}
  \label{fig:danger-quadrant-v2}
\end{figure}

%% --- Intervention: net selective clarification per policy (972 cells) -------
\begin{figure}[t]
  \centering
  \includegraphics[width=0.62\linewidth]{fig_intervention_v2.pdf}
  \caption{Selective clarification (Study~2 intervention, 972 real cells). Net selective
  clarification (appropriate $-$ over-clarification) per gating policy; LPP-gated reaches
  $0.339$, above every baseline. In the danger subset where same-prompt uncertainty is
  blind, LPP covers $0.741$ of AMB$+$ items versus $0.140$ for semantic entropy.}
  \label{fig:intervention-v2}
\end{figure}
